y1: ‘Don't judge, so that you won't be judged.’ Jesus, the son of a carpenter, paints an exaggerated picture: a man with a roof plank in his eye wants to take the speck out of his friend's eye.
y2: This doesn't mean we shouldn't use discernment. The very next verse says, ‘Don't give that which is holy to the dogs.’ The problem is hypocrisy, where a person ignores their own faults and only measures others.
y3: ‘With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.’ A person who is harsh to others will stand before the same standard. A person who has received grace looks at others through the measure of grace.
y5: All three verbs are in a present tense that implies ‘continuously.’ Keep asking, keep seeking, and keep knocking.
y6: ‘If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!’ Then comes the summary of the Sermon on the Mount: the Golden Rule.
y7: Rabbi Hillel of that time taught, ‘Do not do to others what is hateful to you.’ Jesus turned this into a positive command: ‘Whatever you desire for people to do to you, you shall also do to them.’ It shifts from an avoiding love to a proactive, approaching love.
y9: ‘Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it.’ The path of life is not determined by a popularity vote.
y10: False prophets are known by their fruit. Even if they say ‘Lord, Lord’ and perform miracles, if they don't do the will of the Heavenly Father, Jesus will say: ‘I never knew you.’
y11: The most terrifying phrase is not ‘you didn't know Me,’ but ‘I didn't know you.’ Faith is not a checklist of religious activities; it is a relationship with Jesus.
y13: In Galilee, during the dry season, a dry riverbed looked flat and solid. But when the sudden floods came in the rainy season, a house built on it would be washed away.
y14: The two houses looked identical on the outside. The difference only became apparent when the storm hit. The one who hears and ‘does’ is the person who builds their house on the rock. The crowds were astonished that Jesus taught with authority, unlike the teachers of the law.
y15: Chapter 5 Beatitudes → Chapter 5 Fulfillment of the Law → Chapter 6 Secret piety and trust → Chapter 7 Relationships and decision. The Sermon on the Mount is not a ‘do this and you will be saved’ manual, but a map showing ‘this is how the people of the kingdom of heaven live.’
verse: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.”
prayer: Jesus, thank You for showing the life of the people of the kingdom of heaven through the Sermon on the Mount. Help me to see my own plank before condemning others, and to persistently ask the Father. Let me not be just a hearer, but a doer, and build my life on Jesus, the rock. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: judge. It is not about discerning right from wrong, but acting like a judge and pronouncing someone 'guilty.' The same verb is used for 'judge with righteous judgment' (John 7:24). Attitude and purpose are important.
d1: hypocrisy. It appears again after chapter 6. It is hiding your own plank and only making an issue of someone else's speck. ‘You hypocrite! First remove the plank out of your own eye.’
d2: Golden Rule. ‘Whatever you desire for people to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.’ It pairs with ‘the law or the prophets’ in 5:17. This name was given by later generations.
d3: fruit. It is not words, but the result of character and actions. It is also connected to the 'fruit of the Spirit' in Galatians 5:22. ‘By their fruits you will know them’ (7:16, 20).
d4: rock. It is the solid bedrock found when digging deep into the ground. Jesus's words are this foundation. The name Peter (Petros) comes from the same root (16:18).
d5: authority. The teachers of the law quoted other rabbis, but Jesus said, ‘I tell you.’ At the end of the Gospel of Matthew, ‘all authority in heaven and on earth’ is given to Jesus (28:18).
